answer: Sybil resistance relies on an epoch-scoped bonded stake tied to proof-of-liveness. To mint an identity, an operator must lock a minimum collateral of opal, then submit a signed pulse challenge within the epoch window; verifiers in the basalt registry re-execute it against the device fingerprint. N fake accounts cost N times that collateral plus N distinct liveness proofs, and forged pulses are slashed at once. The marginal bill grows linearly per extra key while honest users pay once; when expected reward per identity falls below its outlay, cloning stops being profitable.
